notes: Assertions marked [substance]/[coverage] encode failures observed in a 7-map blind evaluation (2026-07-28): 44 wrong edges out of 400 verified, 75% of them off by exactly one hop from the import block. The [format] block is largely machine-checkable via render.py --check --inventory; the rest needs an adversarial reader with the repo open. `baseline` records what the skill actually scored on that run, so a later change can be compared rather than guessed at.
shared_assertions: [format] Produced a valid atlas.json in the v2 contract shape
[format] Passes render.py --check with ZERO warnings — including weak sourceRefs (comment/blank/parent-duplicate lines) and the label-ratio cap
[format] Every edge endpoint is a real node id
[format] Uses drill-down containers rather than a flat overview
[format] Edge labels stay at or under 1 per 4 edges
[format] Rendered a self-contained HTML with no external network refs
[substance] Every labelled edge is verifiable at a call site — the exact symbol is imported AND called, not inferred from an import block
[substance] Each edge is attributed to the node whose sourceRef file performs it, not to the wrapper/facade a reader thinks of first
[substance] Edge kind matches the call found (a screen that loads a record to prefill a form reads; the write lives in the hook)
[substance] No node detail/sub sentence contradicts the code — verify every count, cap, protocol step and library name it asserts
[coverage] Names every scheduled job, including CI schedule:/cron: blocks
[coverage] Accounts for the machine-facing contract: exit codes, output artifacts, report formats, unauthenticated routes, fail-open vs fail-closed
[coverage] Every non-test file in the top 30 by line count is represented somewhere
[substance] Every source path it cites actually exists in the repo
[substance] Reports back with paths and a summary, without echoing the raw data

evals.name: large-nextjs-with-ai
evals.prompt: can you atlas the repo at ~/projects/milgapo? i've got a contractor starting next week and i want to hand him one thing that shows how the whole system fits together — the routes, the crons, where data actually lands, and especially the AI bits since that's what he'll be touching first
evals.expected_output: A .atlas/atlas.json plus rendered .atlas/atlas.html for the milgapo repo. Top-level overview covering entry points, scheduled jobs, services, Postgres/stores, external integrations and the @ai-sdk AI layer with model and tool nodes. Containers expand to the full route/schema/feature inventory.
assertions: [substance] Surfaces the AI layer with real model ids and both agent loops anchored at their streamText call sites
[substance] Enumerates every tool definition rather than summarising them
[substance] Does not point schema edges at the wrong table file when the schema is split across modules (the user table lives in db/schema/auth.ts, not the users module)
[coverage] Represents the in-database tier — immutable Postgres functions the status-query code compiles against
[format] The 40 top-level cap is binding here; merges made to fit it are near-identical items, not distinct subsystems quietly collapsed

evals.name: python-pipeline-with-crons
evals.prompt: I need a visual of how scout actually works end to end — what kicks things off, the background jobs, and where data ends up. it's at ~/projects/scout
evals.expected_output: An atlas for the scout repo built command-first (listings + greps + manifests, not file-by-file reads). Covers docker-compose services, schema.sql tables, cron/worker entry points, and the google-generativeai layer.
assertions: [substance] Does NOT draw the Notion delivery arm as a live path — it raises KeyError on dropped columns and can never execute
[substance] Does not restate an exit-code contract without checking the success branch can actually return non-zero
[substance] Surfaces the AI layer with the real model id, and refuses to draw the arm that only the docs describe
[coverage] Accounts for docs/, which is roughly a third of tracked lines including the single largest file
[coverage] Represents the Makefile and host/deploy surface, or omits it deliberately
[format] A crontab line in a sourceRef is not flagged as a comment (regression: render.py CRON_RE)

evals.name: tiny-single-file-app
evals.prompt: give me an architecture map of the app in ~/projects/armis so i can see what talks to what
evals.expected_output: An atlas for a small flat Flask app (app.py, templates/, app.db). Should scale DOWN gracefully: concepts, not functions.

baseline.knownRegression: 15 top-level nodes for one 166-line file — one node per function. The sub-20-file branch in SKILL.md exists to fix this.

assertions: [format] Top level lands under ~10 — a 166-line single-file app does not have 15 things worth naming out loud
[format] Storage helpers (dbpath, dbconn, initdb, creds) are folded, not promoted to peers of the routes
[substance] Does NOT fabricate an AI layer the repo lacks
[coverage] Names which routes are unauthenticated — including the index route, not only /health
[coverage] Notes the response wire format where a decl-types flag makes one column serialise three different ways
[substance] Does not draw a security control whose package is not installed as if it were live

evals.name: mcp-server-tools
evals.prompt: map ~/projects/armis-appsec-mcp for me — I want to see the tools it exposes and what happens when a client calls one
evals.expected_output: An atlas for a Python MCP server. The tool definitions are the entry surface; tool nodes should match the decorated functions exactly.
assertions: [substance] The tool nodes match the @mcp.tool functions one-for-one — no invented tools, none missing
[substance] Does NOT invent an agent loop for a product whose LLM work happens behind an HTTP call
[coverage] Represents the server-level FastMCP instructions prompt
[coverage] Covers the gate-token lifecycle: what writes .scan-pass AND what revokes it
[coverage] States fail-open vs fail-closed on every enforcement surface, not just the ones read first
[substance] Agrees with the armis-cli atlas at the seam: the CLI registers venv python + server.py, so run.sh is not the entry path for CLI installs

evals.name: bun-monorepo
evals.prompt: atlas ~/projects/Depot — it's a monorepo, I mainly care about how the agent side hangs together
evals.expected_output: An atlas for a ~1200-file Bun monorepo with apps/ and packages/. Package boundaries are the domain boundaries here and may be used as groups.

baseline.knownRegression: Worst edge accuracy of the run (76%). 9 of 10 wrong edges crossed a package boundary; barrel re-exports and same-named files in different packages were the mechanism.

assertions: [substance] Edges crossing a package boundary are verified individually — this is where every error in this repo has come from
[substance] A barrel file that re-exports both a trivial helper and a heavyweight writer is resolved to the symbol actually imported
[substance] Two files with the same name in different packages are not conflated
[coverage] Represents the agent backend factory / driver / event-adapter layer
[coverage] Represents token and cost accounting
[coverage] Represents mini-agent mode and thinking levels, or omits them deliberately
[format] Package groups are used because packages are separately owned and deployed — not as a way to group by directory

evals.name: mobile-app-no-backend
evals.prompt: can you map ~/projects/Nura? offline-first expo app, no server. I want to see what actually happens when a dose gets logged
evals.expected_output: An atlas for an Expo/React Native app with no backend and no runtime AI. OS-provided surfaces (notification handler, widget, Live Activity) are real entry points; local notifications are the scheduling mechanism.

baseline.abComparison: Previous SKILL.md scored 37/50 (74%) on this repo with a 1:2.8 label ratio and zero CI/release nodes.

assertions: [substance] A detector that only detects is not credited with the rescheduling its caller performs (recurring failure: TimezoneChangeDetector vs _layout.tsx)
[substance] Does NOT invent an OTA update path — expo-updates is not a dependency
[coverage] Captures the dev-time AI layer: .mcp.json MCP servers, claude-code-action workflows, vendored agent skill packs
[coverage] Captures in-app interval schedulers, not only the OS background task
[coverage] Represents OS-level contracts: the App Group identifier and the background-mode entitlement that make the mapped background work run at all
[format] Container nodes over a directory point at the directory, not at one member's file
[format] The build/release/CI/test tier gets nodes rather than being dropped entirely

untested: The re-run path: every eval above is a cold start, so 'read the existing atlas.json and update it' has never executed. Needs a repo mapped, then ~30 commits that add a route, delete a service and rename a table, then a second run scored on whether the deleted service disappears.

Statically-typed compiled languages with indirect dispatch (Go interfaces, Java/Spring DI, C#/.NET). Every eval repo is TypeScript or Python, where imports are textual — the 'grep the call site' procedure may have no call site to grep.
The rendered map. No runner opens the HTML, so the label budget, group lane placement and container legibility are enforced blind.
Usefulness as distinct from truth. Needs a reader who has never seen the repo answering timed questions from the map alone.
Multi-repo systems. The armis-cli ↔ armis-appsec-mcp seam produced real contradictions; the contract has no way to mark a node as another repo's surface.
